hints: Focus on what alkaline aqueous iodine actually tests for, the iodoform reaction and the yellow precipitate of CHI3.

Remember the two groups that give a positive result are the methyl carbonyl group, $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$, and the methyl secondary alcohol group, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$, which is oxidised in situ.
Check each pair to see if one compound has one of those groups and the other does not, because if both are positive or both are negative you cannot distinguish them.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

Great start, let us remember the rule first. Alkaline aqueous iodine gives a yellow precipitate of triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$, with a distinct antiseptic smell.

Positive groups:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{C=O} \text{ and } \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$$

**Check pair 1: butanal and butanone**

Butanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. It has no methyl group attached to the carbonyl, so negative.

Butanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It is a methyl ketone, so positive. One yes and one no, so they can be distinguished.

**Check pair 2: pentan-2-one and pentan-3-ol**

Pentan-2-one is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It is a methyl ketone, so positive.

Pentan-3-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The OH carbon has ethyl groups on both sides, not a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$ group, so negative. Again one yes and one no, so they can be distinguished.

**Check pair 3: propanone and propan-2-ol**

Propanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. It is a methyl ketone, so positive.

Propan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. This contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$ group, which is oxidised by the reagent to a methyl carbonyl and then also gives positive. Both yes, so they cannot be distinguished.

Conclusion: 1 and 2 only can be distinguished.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three pairs. Pair 3 is the trap, both propanone and propan-2-ol give a positive iodoform test, so they cannot be distinguished.
options.B: Correct because only 1 and 2 work. In each of those pairs one compound is positive (butanone and pentan-2-one) and the other is negative (butanal and pentan-3-ol), giving a clear yellow precipitate difference.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes pair 3. Students choosing this often forget that the secondary alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ is also oxidised to give a positive result, just like a methyl ketone.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only pair 1. Students choosing this often think pentan-3-ol will be positive because it is a secondary alcohol, forgetting the test needs specifically a methyl group next to the $\text{CH(OH)}$ carbon.
